- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.2), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 92), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap 30d forecast at +5% above recent peak or use 10-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast mean for 30d horizon.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 90, true outcome often drops 2–5% in next 7d; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for 30d horizon if recent 7d mean is > 90.
- Forecast often lags true price by 2–5 days; if true outcome is rising, model may be 1–2 days behind; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true price.
- For 30d horizon, if sentiment is 0.00 and history shows 3+ consecutive low prices, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid “bottoming” bias.
